requirements.title: Validation rules for workspace names, URLs, branches and durations
requirements.rationale: Every workspace route judges a slug, a URL, a branch name and a duration by the same rule, so the rules are built once.

criteria.action: for any string, accept it as a repository slug exactly when it is 3 to 64 characters long, holds only the letters a to z, digits and hyphens, starts with a letter, ends with a letter or digit and does not contain two hyphens in a row

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/validate_test.go, a table over ValidateSlug: accepted {abc, a1b, my-repo-2, a 64-character slug}; refused {'', ab, a 65-character slug, 1abc, -abc, abc-, a--b, Abc, a_b, a.b, 'a b', 'abç'}; assert the result per row

criteria.action: for any string, accept it as a git_url exactly when it has the form https://<host>/<path> without userinfo or the form git@<host>:<path>, with a non-empty host and a non-empty path, without resolving the host or opening a connection

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/validate_test.go, a table over ValidateGitURL: accepted {https://example.com/a/b.git, https://example.com:8443/a, git@example.com:a/b.git}; refused {'', http://example.com/a, ssh://git@example.com/a, file:///tmp/a, /tmp/a, https://example.com, https://example.com/, https:///a, https://user@example.com/a, https://user:pw@example.com/a, git@example.com:, git@:a, other@example.com:a}; assert the result per row; the host name in every row does not resolve, which proves no lookup happens

criteria.action: for any string, accept it as a branch name exactly when it is not empty, holds no control character, space, ~, ^, :, ?, *, [ or backslash, holds no '..', '//' or '@{', is not exactly '@', does not start with '-' or '/', does not end with '/', '.' or '.lock', and has no path component that starts with '.' or ends with '.lock'

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/validate_test.go, a table over ValidateBranchName: accepted {main, feature/x, fix-42, a.b, a@b, release/1.2}; refused {'', '@', 'a b', a~b, a^b, a:b, a?b, a*b, a[b, a\b, a..b, a//b, a@{b, -a, /a, a/, a., a.lock, .a, a/.b, a.lock/b, a name holding a tab, a name holding byte 0x7f}; assert the result per row

criteria.action: for any string, accept it as a fork name exactly when it is 1 to 32 characters long, holds only the letters a to z, digits and hyphens, starts and ends with a letter or digit and does not contain two hyphens in a row

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/validate_test.go, a table over ValidateForkName: accepted {a, 7, a-b, 1x, a 32-character name}; refused {'', a 33-character name, -a, a-, a--b, A, a_b}; assert the result per row

criteria.action: for any string, parse it as a duration exactly when it is a positive whole number in decimal digits followed by one unit m, h or d, and return the length of time it names

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/validate_test.go, a table over ParseDuration: {90m -> 90 minutes, 24h -> 24 hours, 7d -> 168 hours, 1m -> 1 minute}; refused {'', 0m, 0d, -1h, +1h, 1.5h, 10, 10s, 1h30m, h, ' 5m', 5M}; assert the value or the refusal per row

requirements.title: State preconditions of routes that need the repository
requirements.rationale: A caller must be able to tell 'come back in a moment' from 'this needs repair' from 'this is archived', and must never be refused only because someone else is working.

criteria.condition: a route that needs the repository is asked for a workspace whose maintenance marker is set or whose status is pending or cloning
criteria.action: refuse the request without acting
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_busy

check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/guard_test.go, a table over RequireReady(workspace) with rows {status, marker} -> outcome: {pending, none} -> 409 workspace_busy; {cloning, none} -> 409 workspace_busy; {ready, reclone} -> 409 workspace_busy; {failed, reclone} -> 409 workspace_busy; {ready, archive} -> 409 workspace_busy; {archived, delete} -> 409 workspace_busy; {failed, none} -> 409 workspace_not_ready; {archived, none} -> 409 workspace_archived; {ready, none} -> nil. Assert the returned error's status and error_type per row. Then call RequireReady on one ready workspace from 50 goroutines at once and assert every call returns nil

criteria.condition: a route that needs the repository is asked for a workspace whose status is failed and whose maintenance marker is not set
criteria.action: refuse the request without acting
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_not_ready

criteria.condition: a route that needs the repository is asked for a workspace whose status is archived and whose maintenance marker is not set
criteria.action: refuse the request without acting
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type workspace_archived

criteria.action: for any workspace whose status is ready and whose maintenance marker is not set, let the request pass the state check, however many other requests are running on that workspace
criteria.contract: the guard returns no error

requirements.title: Who may call POST /workspaces
requirements.rationale: A workspace needs a user as owner, and a token must hold the write scope before it can create anything.

criteria.condition: POST /workspaces is called with a personal access token that does not hold the scope workspaces:write
criteria.action: refuse the request and create nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope; no workspace exists afterwards

setup: a workspace service on a temporary store with the real access, secret and event components, served through net/http/httptest
a user U with a personal organization and an API key
check.pseudocode: in internal/workspace/create_test.go, a table over callers posting a valid body: {PAT with no scopes, PAT with only workspaces:read} -> 403 insufficient_scope; {admin token} -> 403 forbidden; {PAT with workspaces:write} -> 201; {API key} -> 201. Then the same refused callers posting the body {} -> the same 403 and error_type, never 400. After every refused row assert the store holds no workspace and the event log no parley.workspace.create

criteria.condition: POST /workspaces is called with the admin token
criteria.action: refuse the request and create nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden; no workspace exists afterwards

criteria.action: for any POST /workspaces request, answer with the first failing check in the order scope, admin-token refusal, body validation, so that a caller refused by scope or as admin token gets the same 403 for a valid and for an invalid body
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with the same error_type for a valid and an invalid body

criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the workspace object: every field present, nullable fields null and never omitted, status pending, access owner

criteria.contract: a user name and password pair, or the value 'no credential'
